svg.title: Shared representation ledger for the Burns-Baylies household in Athens
svg.desc: A documentary ledger separating embassy residence hosting, Elizabeth Baylies-Burns's independent civic work, and her earlier preservation background from the ambassador's formal state authority.
svg.text: The residence was also a representational space.
Shared diplomatic life, distinct roles · 1981–2003 documentary sequence

g.text: Libby Baylies Burns is credited on federal historic-preservation work at West Point and Watertown Arsenal.
Context, not causation: no source currently proves this work directed or caused the Athens embassy renovation.
Nicholas Burns and Elizabeth Baylies-Burns co-host a Gennadeion fundraising dinner; about 50 guests attend.
Contemporaneous institutional record reports $70,000 in pledges. The source attributes the welcome to Burns, not Libby.
Later institutional reporting says MDA Hellas was established with Baylies-Burns's help; Greek reporting names her honorary president.
In 2002 Kathimerini called her an instigator of the specialized neuromuscular-disease unit at Aghia Sophia Children's Hospital.
Shared representation did not give the ambassador's spouse authority to speak for U.S. policy. Civic work remains her record, not his.

svg.text: Sources: ASCSA Gennadeion records; Kathimerini; MDA Hellas retrospective; HABS/HAER and Library of Congress project records.
